sal.basis: Senior Financial Analyst / FP&A, ~8 yrs, Warsaw, employment contract (umowa o pracę), base pay excluding bonus: about PLN 16,000 gross a month (~PLN 192k a year). Basis: prior knowledge of 2025 recruiter salary guides for Poland (Hays, Michael Page, Robert Walters), not re-verified live because the search budget was used up and direct fetches are blocked here: senior financial / FP&A analysts in Warsaw roughly PLN 12,000-18,000 gross a month, FP&A managers roughly PLN 18,000-28,000; Kraków and Wrocław business-services roles 5-15% lower. Polish pay is quoted brutto per month (B2B as netto + VAT), so per=month. f = 16,000 / 26,000 = 0.615, so Noura's 26,000 SAR maps to ~PLN 16,000 and her 34,000 SAR expectation to ~PLN 20,900, the entry FP&A-manager band.

sensitive.notes: Polish CVs very often carry a photo, but it is not required. A photo is outside the data an employer may demand from candidates (Labour Code art. 22¹), so it is given voluntarily and covered by consent (art. 22¹a); we allow one but never ask for it. Art. 22¹ does let employers ask for name, date of birth, contact details, education, qualifications and work history, but online application forms (Pracuj.pl, ATS forms) normally ask only for name, contact details and the CV, and art. 18³a bans discrimination on grounds including sex, age and nationality, so we do not ask for date of birth, gender, nationality or marital status. Right to work is asked instead of nationality. Many employers still expect a GDPR (RODO) consent clause at the foot of the CV; since the May 2019 amendments it is legally needed only for future recruitments or extra data such as a photo, but it is the norm, so Polish CVs get the standard clause.

legal.law: GDPR (RODO) + Polish Personal Data Protection Act of 10 May 2018

culture.notes: Mon-Fri, 40-hour week (8 hours a day); hybrid with 2-3 office days is common at Warsaw, Kraków and Wrocław corporates and business-services centres. Pay is discussed as gross per month (brutto) on an employment contract (umowa o pracę); B2B contracts quoted as net + VAT are common in tech and some senior finance roles, so always say which a figure is. Pay is monthly, no later than the 10th of the following month (Labour Code art. 85), often at month end; there is no statutory 13th salary in the private sector, but annual bonuses are common. Since 24 Dec 2025 employers must tell candidates the pay or pay range before the interview and may not ask about current or past pay. Statutory notice on a permanent contract depends on tenure with the current employer (art. 36): 2 weeks under 6 months, 1 month from 6 months, 3 months from 3 years, so experienced hires usually have 3 months; an earlier exit by mutual agreement (porozumienie stron) is often negotiated. CV: 1-2 pages, reverse chronological, photo common but optional, and many employers still expect a RODO consent clause at the bottom. A cover letter (list motywacyjny) is optional except at some public bodies. Polish is required at most domestic employers; English is the working language at multinationals and business-services centres, where German or another EU language is a plus.
